$comment: Permission overlay for the overnight loop. Launch with:
DENY-ONLY, on purpose. An allow-list here would be a third copy of what the repo already
decides twice -- once in CLAUDE.md's deny-list and once in the branch ruleset -- and the one
that silently stops covering its family the moment a tool is added. Deny entries only ever
subtract, so a stale one costs a prompt, never a breach.
The source system's own unattended profile is the cautionary tale: it denied every
`gh pr merge`, which is the exact command its loop's merge step runs, and its test suite
pinned that behaviour. Nothing here may deny a command the loop itself must issue -- so
`gh pr merge --auto` is deliberately NOT denied. The gate that stops a bad merge is the branch
ruleset, server-side, which no client setting can talk its way past.
